screening_decisions.reason: Methodological paper discussing case-control study designs, not an actual diagnostic accuracy study of echocardiography for PH detection.
Registry study describing prevalence and clinical characteristics of PAH patients, not a diagnostic accuracy study comparing echocardiography to RHC.
Single-gate design studying only patients with known PAH; no control group without PH. Does not provide TP/FP/TN/FN data for diagnostic accuracy.

Evaluates diagnostic accuracy of Doppler echocardiography vs RHC for PH detection. Uses mPAP≥25.5 mmHg threshold (very close to 25 mmHg). Provides sensitivity (98%) and specificity (100%) data from which TP/FP/TN/FN can be derived.

Large unselected cohort (792 pairs) comparing echo PASP to RHC. Reports misclassification rate (54.4%). While TP/FP/TN/FN not explicitly stated, data may be extractable from full text. Conservative inclusion.
Compares echo to Swan-Ganz catheter in HF patients. Reports sensitivity and specificity calculations. Threshold not explicitly stated but may use standard 25 mmHg. Data potentially extractable.
Reports correlation (r=0.90) and standard error but does not provide TP/FP/TN/FN data or diagnostic accuracy metrics for PH detection.
Uses mPAP≥25 mmHg threshold with RHC reference. Evaluates composite index including echo data. May contain extractable echo-specific diagnostic accuracy data. Conservative inclusion.
Focuses on acute pulmonary embolism diagnosis (n=9), not PH detection. Does not provide TP/FP/TN/FN data for PH diagnostic accuracy.
Completely unrelated topic - pregnancy outcomes and placental function, not pulmonary hypertension or echocardiography.
Unselected population (n=177) comparing DE to RHC. Focuses on factors affecting accuracy but may contain underlying diagnostic accuracy data. Conservative inclusion.
Uses mPAP>35 mmHg threshold instead of required 25 mmHg. Different clinical question (ruling out significant POPH).
Uses PASP≥30 mmHg threshold instead of required mPAP≥25 mmHg. Different pressure parameter and threshold.
Focuses on PVR estimation accuracy, not PH diagnostic accuracy. Does not provide TP/FP/TN/FN for PH detection.
Uses mPAP>20 mmHg threshold instead of required 25 mmHg. Different threshold makes it ineligible.
Meta-analysis pooling data from other studies, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
Epidemiological study of PAH incidence/prevalence, not a diagnostic accuracy study.
Review article discussing definitions and diagnosis, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
Large study (n=307 with both tests within 5 days) comparing echo to RHC. Uses mPAP≥25 mmHg threshold. Reports AUC for classifying PH (0.97 for RVSP). Diagnostic accuracy data available.
Title indicates focus on congestive heart failure assessment, not PH detection. Abstract provides no relevant information.

This study describes a new contactless cardiovascular monitoring technique (DUiFK-P system) and does not evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of trans-thoracic Doppler echocardiography for detecting pulmonary hypertension. No RHC reference standard is used, and no diagnostic accuracy data (TP/FP/TN/FN) is provided.

While this study compares Doppler echocardiography to RHC in patients with PH, it only provides correlation coefficients and Bland-Altman agreement analysis. No diagnostic accuracy data (TP/FP/TN/FN or sensitivity/specificity) is provided that would allow extraction of the 2x2 table required for meta-analysis.

This is a guideline document providing updated recommendations for cardiac chamber quantification. It is not a primary diagnostic accuracy study evaluating Doppler echocardiography for PH detection against RHC.

This appears to be a commentary/editorial discussing another study. It mentions ePASP > 47 mmHg threshold (not 25 mmHg) and does not provide TP/FP/TN/FN data. The study design and data requirements are not met.

This study compares two methods of measuring tricuspid regurgitant velocity (chin vs beard) in patients undergoing RHC. It is a method comparison study, not a diagnostic accuracy study for PH detection. No TP/FP/TN/FN data is provided.

While this study uses RHC with mean PAP ≥25mmHg threshold and provides AUC values, it compares two echocardiographic parameters (TAPSE/RVSP vs RVSL) rather than evaluating Doppler echocardiography alone for PH detection. No TP/FP/TN/FN data is provided.

This is a prognostic study examining the association between PASP assessed by Doppler echocardiography and mortality in heart failure patients. It does not use RHC as a reference standard and does not evaluate diagnostic accuracy for PH detection.

This study uses RHC as reference but defines PH as mean PAP >20 mmHg, which differs from the required 25 mmHg threshold. Additionally, it evaluates exercise Doppler echocardiography rather than standard resting Doppler echocardiography.

This study evaluates Doppler echocardiography against RHC (reference standard) with PH defined as mean PA pressure ≥25 mmHg (correct threshold). It provides data from which TP/FP/TN/FN can be extracted: 'Echo classified 38 subjects correctly (14/24 with and 24/25 without PH)' giving TP=14, FN=10, TN=24, FP=1. Sensitivity 58%, specificity 96% are also reported.

While this study uses RHC as reference and examines Doppler echocardiography in patients with chronic lung disease, it only provides correlation coefficients and positive predictive value (84% for AcT < 90 msec). No TP/FP/TN/FN data or sensitivity/specificity is provided.

This study compares three formulas for PASP estimation against RHC but only provides correlation coefficients. No diagnostic accuracy data (TP/FP/TN/FN or sensitivity/specificity) is provided for PH detection.
This study focuses on estimating left ventricular end-diastolic pressure (LVEDP), not pulmonary hypertension detection. The outcome of interest is different from the review objective.

This study uses PAPs ≥35 mmHg as the threshold for pulmonary arterial hypertension, which differs from the required 25 mmHg threshold. Additionally, it only provides correlation data without TP/FP/TN/FN values.

This study evaluates tissue Doppler imaging (TDI) parameters, not standard trans-thoracic Doppler echocardiography. While it uses the correct 25 mmHg threshold and RHC reference, it only provides sensitivity/specificity (~70%) without TP/FP/TN/FN data.

This study evaluates echocardiography for monitoring hemodynamic deterioration in patients with known PAH, not for initial detection/diagnosis of PH. The review objective is to determine diagnostic accuracy for detecting PH, not monitoring disease progression.
This study evaluates ECG, NT-proBNP, oxygen saturation, and WHO functional class for PH prediction, not Doppler echocardiography. The index test does not match the review protocol.

While this study compares echocardiography to RHC in pregnant women, it only provides correlation coefficients (rho=0.79). No diagnostic accuracy data (TP/FP/TN/FN or sensitivity/specificity) is provided.

This study uses PASP > 50 mmHg as the threshold for clinically significant pulmonary hypertension, which differs from the required 25 mmHg threshold. It only provides PPV (37.5%) and NPV (91.9%) without TP/FP/TN/FN data.

While this study evaluates various echocardiographic parameters against RHC and provides some sensitivity/specificity values (e.g., 0.85/0.5 for pulmonary acceleration time), it does not provide TP/FP/TN/FN data that can be extracted for meta-analysis.

This is a prognostic/predictor study examining characteristics and predictors of PH in emphysema patients. While it uses RHC with mPAP > 25 mmHg threshold, it does not evaluate diagnostic accuracy of Doppler echocardiography and provides no TP/FP/TN/FN data.

Study evaluates accuracy of Doppler echocardiography for estimating pulmonary artery pressure using Bland-Altman analysis, but does not provide TP/FP/TN/FN values for PH diagnosis. Focuses on pressure estimation accuracy rather than diagnostic accuracy for PH detection.
Study focuses on pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) estimation, not PH detection. Uses PVR thresholds (6 and 8 Wood units) rather than mPAP 25 mmHg threshold for PH diagnosis.

Study uses RHC as reference standard with mPAP > 25 mmHg threshold for PH diagnosis. Reports sensitivity (59%) and specificity (78%) for ePASP cut-off. Diagnostic accuracy data may be extractable from reported metrics and sample size (n=31 liver transplant patients). Conservative inclusion pending full-text review.
Study compares echocardiographic algorithms for PH estimation but reports only odds ratios and correlations. No TP/FP/TN/FN values or 2x2 table data provided for diagnostic accuracy assessment.
Study uses MPAP > 45 mmHg threshold for severe PH, not the required 25 mmHg threshold for PH diagnosis. Does not provide TP/FP/TN/FN values for PH detection at 25 mmHg threshold.
Study uses mean pulmonary artery pressure > 20 mmHg threshold, not the required 25 mmHg threshold for PH diagnosis. Does not provide TP/FP/TN/FN values.
Study compares three Doppler methods for PAP prediction but reports only correlation coefficients. No TP/FP/TN/FN values or 2x2 table data provided for diagnostic accuracy assessment.

Study uses RHC as reference standard in 374 lung transplant candidates. Reports sensitivity (85%), specificity (55%), PPV (52%), and NPV (87%) for PH diagnosis. Diagnostic accuracy data may be extractable from reported metrics and sample size. Conservative inclusion pending full-text review.
Study focuses on occult diastolic dysfunction detection, not PH detection. Primary outcome is diastolic dysfunction identified at catheterization with fluid challenge, not PH diagnosis.

Study uses RHC as reference standard with mPAP > 25 mmHg threshold for PH diagnosis. Reports likelihood ratios (PLR 4.7, NLR 0.12) for PH detection. Diagnostic accuracy data may be extractable from reported metrics and sample size (n=118). Conservative inclusion pending full-text review.
Population-based cohort study using echocardiography only without RHC reference standard. Does not meet criterion requiring RHC as reference standard for PH diagnosis.

Study uses RHC as reference standard with mPAP >= 25 mmHg threshold for PH diagnosis. Reports sensitivity (95%) and specificity (33%) for RVSP cutoff. Diagnostic accuracy data may be extractable from reported metrics and sample size (n=30). Conservative inclusion pending full-text review.
Study evaluates plasma interleukin-6 for sepsis diagnosis, not PH detection. Completely different topic and population.

Study assesses accuracy of echocardiography-based formulas for mPAP estimation but reports only correlation coefficients (rs=0.909, 0.904). No TP/FP/TN/FN values or 2x2 table data provided for diagnostic accuracy assessment.
Study is a treatment algorithm review for PAH, not a diagnostic accuracy study. Does not evaluate diagnostic accuracy of echocardiography for PH detection.
Study is a methodological review about search filters for DTA studies, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study for PH detection.
Study uses PAP >= 20 mmHg threshold for PH diagnosis, not the required 25 mmHg threshold. Does not provide TP/FP/TN/FN values.
Study evaluates echocardiography for LVRS patient selection but reports only correlation (r=-0.29). No TP/FP/TN/FN values or 2x2 table data provided for diagnostic accuracy assessment.
Study reports inaccuracy rate (19.7%) and that 1 in 3 patients with HRPAH was missed, but does not provide TP/FP/TN/FN values or 2x2 table data for diagnostic accuracy assessment.

Study correlates Doppler measurements with catheterization but reports only correlation coefficients (r=0.97, 0.96, 0.95). No TP/FP/TN/FN values or 2x2 table data provided for diagnostic accuracy assessment.

Study reports only correlation coefficients (r values) between Doppler echocardiography and cardiac catheterisation. No diagnostic accuracy data (TP, FP, TN, FN values) provided. Does not meet the requirement for sufficient diagnostic test accuracy data.

Study focuses on detecting increased pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR > 3 WU) rather than PH defined by mPAP >= 25 mmHg. Uses PASP > 40 mmHg threshold, not the required 25 mmHg mPAP threshold. Does not meet the reference standard threshold criterion.
This is a review article discussing MR and CT imaging for PH evaluation, not a diagnostic accuracy study of Doppler echocardiography. Does not meet the study design requirement.

Study reports that 'an optimal RVSP threshold for the screening of PH could not be detected' and does not provide clear TP/FP/TN/FN values. While RHC is used as reference, insufficient diagnostic accuracy data is provided to extract 2x2 table values.
Abstract describes the SWEDEHEART registry system, not a diagnostic accuracy study of echocardiography for PH detection. Does not meet the study design requirement.
This is a review article about riociguat treatment for PH, not a diagnostic accuracy study of echocardiography. Does not meet the study design requirement.

Study reports only correlation coefficient (R = 0.58) between echocardiography and RHC. No diagnostic accuracy data (TP, FP, TN, FN values) provided. Does not meet the requirement for sufficient diagnostic test accuracy data.

Study evaluates diagnostic accuracy of TTE vs RHC for detecting PH. Provides sensitivity (92.8%, 94.1%) and specificity (86.6%, 73.3%) values. RHC is used as reference standard. While the exact threshold is not explicitly stated as 25 mmHg, the study provides sufficient diagnostic accuracy data. Conservative approach to include for full-text review.

Study uses MRI myocardial tagging to assess interventricular asynchrony in PAH patients, not diagnostic accuracy of Doppler echocardiography for PH detection. Does not meet the index test requirement.
Study compares PC-MRI to RHC and echocardiography, with MRI as the primary index test. Not a diagnostic accuracy study of Doppler echocardiography. Does not meet the index test requirement.

Study evaluates diagnostic accuracy of Doppler echocardiography vs RHC. Uses mPAP >= 25 mmHg threshold (correct threshold). Provides AUC values (0.92 for sPAP to predict mPAP >= 25 mmHg). RHC is reference standard. Provides sufficient diagnostic accuracy data for potential 2x2 table extraction.

Study evaluates diagnostic accuracy of echocardiography vs cardiac catheterization for PH detection. Uses mPAP >= 25 mmHg threshold (correct threshold). Provides sensitivity (92.3%, 62.2%, 77.1%), specificity (81.8%, 89.3%, 66.7%), and AUC values. RHC is reference standard. Provides sufficient diagnostic accuracy data.

Study uses SPAP >= 30 mmHg threshold for screening, not the required mPAP >= 25 mmHg threshold. While it provides sensitivity (100%) and specificity (82%), the reference standard threshold differs from the protocol requirement.

Study uses MPAP >= 35 mmHg threshold for moderate to severe PH, not the required mPAP >= 25 mmHg threshold. While it provides sensitivity (97%) and specificity (77%), the reference standard threshold differs from the protocol requirement.

Study evaluates diagnostic accuracy of Doppler echocardiography vs RHC. Provides sensitivity (81%) and specificity (69%) for predicting PH. RHC is reference standard. While the exact threshold is not explicitly stated, the study provides sufficient diagnostic accuracy data. Conservative approach to include for full-text review.
Study describes epidemiology and survival of incident PAH patients, not diagnostic accuracy of echocardiography. Does not meet the study design requirement.
Study develops a survival prediction tool for PAH patients, not a diagnostic accuracy study of echocardiography. Does not meet the study design requirement.

Study reports only correlation coefficients between echo-Doppler parameters and mPAP. No diagnostic accuracy data (TP, FP, TN, FN values) provided. Does not meet the requirement for sufficient diagnostic test accuracy data.

Abstract describes a study on mechanical dyssynchrony assessment in cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) candidates, not diagnostic accuracy of echocardiography for PH detection. Title does not match abstract content. Does not meet the study design requirement.

Study reports only correlation coefficients between Doppler indices and pulmonary artery pressure/distensibility. No diagnostic accuracy data (TP, FP, TN, FN values) provided. Does not meet the requirement for sufficient diagnostic test accuracy data.

While this study evaluates echocardiography for PAH detection using RHC as reference standard, it does not provide sufficient diagnostic test accuracy data (TP, FP, TN, FN values). Only AUC (0.72) is reported without contingency table data.
This is a registry study examining factors associated with delayed PAH recognition, not a diagnostic accuracy study evaluating echocardiography. Does not meet the primary objective of the review.

Study uses RHC as reference standard with mPAP≥25mmHg threshold, but provides only correlation coefficients and Bland-Altman analysis without explicit TP/FP/TN/FN values or sensitivity/specificity data needed for meta-analysis.
This study examines the effectiveness/outcomes of RHC use in ICU patients, not the diagnostic accuracy of echocardiography for PH detection. Completely different research question.

Uses sPAP cut-off of 36 mmHg instead of the required 25 mmHg threshold for PH definition. While sensitivity (87%) and specificity (79%) are reported, they are based on incorrect threshold per protocol requirements.

Focuses on right ventricular afterload assessment including PAMP and PA pressure waveform, not specifically on PH detection diagnostic accuracy. No TP/FP/TN/FN or sensitivity/specificity data provided.

Meets all criteria: evaluates Doppler echocardiography for PH detection, uses cardiac catheterization as reference standard, uses mPAP≥25mmHg threshold, and provides sensitivity (100%), specificity (88%), and PPV (30%). Single-gate design (consecutive liver transplant candidates).
This is a methodological paper describing the QUADAS-2 quality assessment tool, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. Not eligible for inclusion.
Focuses on right atrial pressure (RAP) estimation accuracy, not on PH detection. Different index test and outcome than required by the review protocol.
This is a consensus/guideline paper updating the clinical classification of PH, not a diagnostic accuracy study. Not eligible for inclusion.

Meets all criteria: evaluates echocardiographic parameters (PR gradient, PAT) for PH detection, uses RHC as reference standard, uses mPAP≥25mmHg threshold, and provides sensitivity (60.8%), specificity (82.4%), and AUC (76.8) from 353 patients.

While it compares echo to RHC, it reports only bias and limits of agreement from Bland-Altman analysis without providing TP/FP/TN/FN values or sensitivity/specificity data needed for diagnostic accuracy meta-analysis.
This is a review article summarizing current knowledge about Doppler diagnosis of PH, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. Reviews are excluded from this systematic review.

This is a screening algorithm/prevalence study that reports PAH prevalence (7.85%) but does not provide complete diagnostic accuracy data (TP/FP/TN/FN or sensitivity/specificity) for echocardiography alone.
Abstract is too brief and provides no diagnostic accuracy data (TP/FP/TN/FN, sensitivity, specificity). Cannot determine if study meets inclusion criteria without full text.

Meets all criteria: evaluates Doppler echocardiography for PAH detection, uses RHC as reference standard, provides sensitivity (100%, 72.7%) and specificity (100%, 63.6%) for echo. Single-gate cross-sectional design in scleroderma patients.

Meets all criteria: evaluates Doppler echocardiography for PH detection, uses invasive measurements as reference standard, uses mPAP≥25mmHg threshold, and reports 100% sensitivity and specificity at defined cutoffs. Prospective observational design.

Meets all criteria: evaluates echocardiography for PH detection, uses RHC as reference standard, uses WHO definitions (mPAP≥25mmHg), and provides sensitivity (60%), specificity (74%), PPV (68%), and NPV (67%).

While it correlates echo with RHC using mPAP≥25mmHg threshold, it reports only correlation coefficients (R=0.80, 0.72, 0.54) without providing TP/FP/TN/FN values or sensitivity/specificity data needed for meta-analysis.
Reports only correlation coefficients (r=0.96) between CW Doppler and CATH measurements without providing diagnostic accuracy data (TP/FP/TN/FN, sensitivity, specificity) for PH detection.
Uses SPAP >35 mmHg or mean pressure >20 mmHg as PH threshold, not the required 25 mmHg mean PAP threshold. Does not report TP/FP/TN/FN values.
Focuses on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, not trans-thoracic Doppler echocardiography. No diagnostic accuracy data provided.
This is a clinical practice guideline document, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. No abstract available.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. Does not provide individual study TP/FP/TN/FN data.
Reports correlation coefficients between echo and RHC measurements but does not provide TP/FP/TN/FN values or clear diagnostic accuracy data.
Uses different thresholds (32.5 mmHg for Chagas, 35.5 mmHg for non-Chagas) instead of the required 25 mmHg mean PAP threshold.
Uses RHC as reference standard with MPAP >25 mmHg threshold. Reports sensitivity (89%) and specificity (84%) for AT cut-off. May have extractable 2x2 data from subgroup of 29 patients.
Reports correlation and positive predictive value but does not provide sufficient TP/FP/TN/FN data for diagnostic accuracy analysis.
Uses RHC as reference standard. Reports 17 screen-positive (10 confirmed, 7 ruled out) and states 'no false negatives'. Partial 2x2 data may be extractable from 165 patients.
Uses RHC as reference standard. Reports sensitivity (97%) and specificity (83%) for MPAP detection of PH. 2x2 data may be calculable from 115 patients.
About Helicobacter pylori diagnostic tests, completely unrelated to pulmonary hypertension or echocardiography.
Retrospective chart review including only patients with TRV >= 2.5 m/s who had RHC - this is a two-gate design (case-control) which is excluded per protocol.
Uses RHC as reference standard with mPAP >= 25 mmHg threshold. Reports AUROC curves for 5 formulae. 2x2 data may be extractable from 33 patients.
Abstract appears truncated/incomplete. Title suggests relevant topic (detection of PH with Doppler echocardiography). Full text needed to assess eligibility.
Uses sPAP cutoff values (30 mmHg and 38 mmHg) instead of the required 25 mmHg mean PAP threshold. Different pressure parameter measured.
Abstract only contains conclusion section. Title suggests comparison of echo vs RHC for PH. Full text needed to assess eligibility and data availability.
Review article about emergency management of PAH patients, not a diagnostic accuracy study of echocardiography.
Uses mPAP >20 mmHg threshold (newer definition) instead of the required 25 mmHg threshold. Also uses exercise echocardiography, not resting.
Uses RHC as reference standard with mPAP >= 25 mmHg threshold. Reports sensitivity (93%), specificity (67%), PPV (91%), NPV (73%). 2x2 data can be calculated from 64 patients.
Methodological paper about bivariate meta-analysis techniques, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study of echocardiography for PH.

Meta-analysis pooling results from 9 primary articles; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. Cannot extract individual TP/FP/TN/FN values from pooled sensitivity/specificity estimates. Excluded per protocol as secondary research.

Retrospective study using logistic regression to predict portopulmonary hypertension (PoPH); does not provide TP/FP/TN/FN diagnostic accuracy data for TTE vs RHC comparison. Uses categorical RVSP ranges rather than binary diagnostic classification.

Systematic review of prognostic factors (hospitalizations/mortality) in PH-LHD patients; not a diagnostic accuracy study of TTE for PH detection. Reviews 45 studies but does not provide primary diagnostic accuracy data.

Evaluates composite diagnostic criteria (6 clinical/lab/imaging findings) rather than TTE alone vs RHC. Likely two-gate design (83 with PH, 472 without PH selected separately). Does not provide TP/FP/TN/FN for TTE diagnostic accuracy.
Uses new PH threshold of 20 mmHg (from 6th World Symposium) instead of required 25 mmHg reference standard threshold. Explicitly excluded per protocol criteria.

Abstract truncated/incomplete; cannot determine eligibility from available information. Title suggests diagnostic accuracy study of TTE for PH. Conservative approach to include for full-text review per protocol guidance.
Review/opinion article discussing integration of invasive and noninvasive tests; no primary diagnostic accuracy data or TP/FP/TN/FN values. Does not evaluate TTE diagnostic accuracy against RHC.

Focuses on pressure-flow relationship during exercise (TPR, P/Q slope ≥3 mmHg/L/min), not PH diagnosis at rest using 25 mmHg threshold. Different outcome measure; does not provide TP/FP/TN/FN for binary PH classification.

Case series of only 21 patients with confirmed precapillary PH; no control group without PH. Cannot calculate diagnostic accuracy (no TN/FN possible). Correlation/agreement study, not diagnostic accuracy study.

Prevalence study of PH in SSc; uses RHC to confirm PH but does not evaluate TTE diagnostic accuracy or provide TP/FP/TN/FN data. Focuses on prevalence and risk factors, not diagnostic test performance.

Bland-Altman agreement study focusing on precision/limits of agreement; explicitly states TTE 'cannot be used for individual diagnosis of pulmonary hypertension'. No TP/FP/TN/FN values provided; reports continuous measurement agreement only.

Examines association between absence of TRV signal and PH prevalence; does not provide diagnostic accuracy data (TP/FP/TN/FN) for TTE performance. Reports PH prevalence in patients with/without TRV, not test accuracy metrics.
Focuses on PVR estimation, not PH diagnosis. Outcome is continuous PVR values (Wood units), not binary PH classification at 25 mmHg threshold. Correlation and Bland-Altman analysis only.

Meets all criteria: TTE vs RHC for PH diagnosis, uses 25 mmHg threshold, reports sensitivity (88%), specificity (83%), accuracy (86%) from which TP/FP/TN/FN can be calculated (n=310). Single-gate design with consecutive patients.

Small study (n=41) in cardiac defect patients only; uses categorical grouping (normal/moderate/high) rather than binary classification at 25 mmHg threshold. Insufficient TP/FP/TN/FN data; reports 85% correct classification only.
